# Snow AU — master assistant context

**ESTABLISHED source:** the author's Snow AU dossier. This context is private author reference, not a package of facts every viewer already knows. Consult STORY_BIBLE, TIMELINE, CONTINUITY_NOTES and approved chapters before future writing. This preparation task authorizes no chapter generation.

Young Coriolanus Snow, based on Tom Blyth's portrayal, lives in the AOT world and now publicly uses **Edmund Voss**. He and Levi were genuine lovers and cohabited in the Underground. Snow was more openly affectionate; Levi welcomed and reciprocated it. Preserve their real happiness alongside Snow's later ruthlessness.

Snow's harmful choices affecting other people caused the permanent breakup. Levi could have killed him, spared him, arranged a way aboveground and said never to return. Levi meant a permanent end; Snow did not accept it. The exact triggering incident and harmed people remain UNRESOLVED.

They have been apart eight years: three peaceful village years, then news that Levi is alive and Humanity's Strongest, then five years building wealth, connections and the Voss identity. Village occupation, precise political office and exact dates require approval. The first-meeting dating wording is inconsistent; do not invent a fix.

The story's watching-room opening is immediately before **Eren's military trial**, where Snow legitimately attends as a political representative. Both men recognize each other immediately. Erwin and Hange can notice Levi's reaction without knowing its history. **Erwin and Levi are NOT a couple**; they have growing trust and emotional closeness.

Snow believes he is coming home, not seeking revenge. His warmth and love are sincere, yet can coexist with possessiveness and entitlement. Levi is not waiting for him and owes no reunion, forgiveness or touch. Do not confuse a stronger public position with moral repair or make Voss politically omnipotent.

Reveal history gradually through footage, observations and Candy's selective revelations; no instant shared omniscience or total backstory dump. Levi keeps his own memories. Other viewers do not know his past automatically. The complete Snow room roster and Snow's room membership are UNRESOLVED. The source's generic pre-expedition opening does not override the Snow pre-trial opening.

Use the general AOT bible for compatible voices and *Power to Strive* for reference structure, not Snow chapter canon or copied prose. Do not import unrelated app AU characters, relationships, body swaps, families or memories.

**Chapter status:** no approved Snow Chapter One or chapter export supplied. Do not reconstruct or replace it. Latest approved chapter and next planned chapter are UNRESOLVED. Do not write continuation chapters until their exact sources and scope are confirmed.

Source authority: current author instructions → Snow AU-specific dossier → compatible general character bible. Source suggestions remain PROPOSED, questions UNRESOLVED, and only explicit author rejection earns DISCARDED.

# Story bible

Source of AU-specific facts: [Snow AU original](archives/originals/1-Snow-AU-.pdf), titled **MASTER CHARACTER AND RELATIONSHIP DOSSIER — CORIOLANUS SNOW / EDMUND VOSS**. Section references below refer to that dossier. No finalized Snow chapter text was supplied.

## Premise and setting — ESTABLISHED

Coriolanus Snow, based on young Snow as portrayed by Tom Blyth in *The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes*, exists within the world of *Attack on Titan*. Write neither elderly President Snow nor a generic omnipotent villain. How he came to exist in this setting is **UNRESOLVED**; the dossier does not establish a transport mechanism or import Panem's institutions. [I–II, pp. 1–4]

Snow and Levi were genuine lovers and lived together in the Underground. Their life included safety, mutual competence, affection and ordinary domestic happiness. Snow was the more openly affectionate partner; Levi welcomed and reciprocated his touch. Their relationship was not manipulation from the outset. [III, pp. 4–8]

Snow's growing ruthlessness and willingness to sacrifice others made their values incompatible. Levi did not fear Snow would kill him. In their final confrontation Levi could have killed him, but could not bring himself to do it. Levi provided a way aboveground and explicitly told Snow never to return. Levi meant a permanent breakup; Snow failed to accept that permanence. [IV, pp. 8–10]

The present reunion occurs eight years after the separation. Snow spent the first three years living peacefully in a village, then learned Levi was alive and known as Captain Levi, Humanity's Strongest Soldier. He spent the following five years building influence and a respectable identity, **Edmund Voss**. Voss is the same person, not another personality. [I; V–VI, pp. 1–2, 11–15]

Voss is a political adviser and representative connected to the Crown's administrative circles. His influence comes from competence, reputation and connections, not unlimited command over the Crown or military. His exact office and responsibilities require approval. [VI, pp. 13–15; XIII]

He and Levi reunite at Eren Yeager's military trial, which Snow attends for legitimate political reasons. Both recognize each other immediately. Snow is genuinely delighted; Levi's recognition is subtle but certain. Erwin and Hange can notice his reaction without knowing its cause. [VII, pp. 15–18]

Erwin and Levi **are not a couple**. They have considerable trust and growing emotional closeness, with no established romantic relationship. Snow can admire and respect Erwin before interpreting him as a rival. [VII.4; XII.21–23]

## Emotional and narrative rules — ESTABLISHED

The dossier's central statement is preserved verbatim:

> Snow believes that he and Levi have a future.
>
> Levi believes that they had a past.

[X, pp. 22–23]

Snow returns because he believes he is coming home, not to exact revenge. His love, warmth, possessiveness and capacity for harm coexist. Greater money and status do not demonstrate that he understands or has repaired his moral failures. Levi is not waiting for him and owes neither forgiveness nor renewed intimacy. Old consent does not confer present permission. [I–II; VIII; X]

The watching-room story begins **immediately before Eren's trial**. Viewers learn through footage, selective revelations by Candy and their own observations. Private thoughts and memories may be revealed selectively; no single opening exposition dump should explain everything. [VII.1; XI, pp. 23–24]

The general character bible's starting point, approximately two days before the 57th Expedition, conflicts with this AU-specific starting point and is superseded for Snow. Preserve each character's actual personal knowledge; never treat dossier text, reference fiction or another character's memories as shared room knowledge.

## Unapproved options — PROPOSED

The village job might be teaching, administration or civic work. Teaching is described as an interesting possibility, not a decision. Money and supplies in Levi's farewell assistance are possible additions, while providing a way aboveground is established. Suggested habits, sample greetings and possible remembered domestic gestures are characterization examples, not completed chapter events. [III.3–4; IV.4; V; VII.3; IX]

## Missing decisions — UNRESOLVED

The precise breakup incident, harmed people, exact dialogue, first-meeting details, village occupation, official office, trial remit, first private reunion conversation, reveal order and full watching-room roster require approval. See [OPEN_QUESTIONS.md](OPEN_QUESTIONS.md).

No supplied idea or draft is classified **DISCARDED**. Explicit “do not” rules constrain characterization; they do not prove that a rejected draft once existed.

# Timeline

Reference point **T0** is Eren Yeager's military trial and the onscreen reunion. No calendar year, exact date or character age has been established in the supplied dossier. Do not supply those from canon assumptions.

| Relative order | Status | Event | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Underground period, before the permanent separation | ESTABLISHED | Snow and Levi meet, become partners and lovers, share a home and experience genuine happiness. | III |
| Later in their relationship | ESTABLISHED | Snow increasingly sacrifices other people and their values diverge. | IV.1–2 |
| Approximately T0 minus eight years | ESTABLISHED | Final confrontation; Levi spares Snow, arranges a way aboveground and tells him never to return. Levi means a permanent end; Snow misreads it. | I; IV |
| First three years after separation | ESTABLISHED | Snow builds a real, peaceful village life with work, routines and friendships. This is not uninterrupted obsession. | V, Years 1–3 |

## Dating conflicts requiring care

**UNRESOLVED:** III.1 says they met “Eight years before the present,” while I, IV–V and XII establish a meaningful shared relationship followed by eight years apart. Do not silently make the meeting and breakup the same date or compress away their relationship. The duration of their courtship/cohabitation and exact meeting date need the author.

**UNRESOLVED wording:** X says Snow spent eight years constructing his return narrative, while V explicitly gives him three genuinely peaceful village years before five years of deliberate reinvention. Preserve the concrete three-plus-five sequence; ask whether X describes retrospective self-justification rather than an eight-year active campaign.

**PROPOSED:** Once Chapter One is supplied, maintain a scene-by-scene record of screen date/order and room revelation order separately. Historical facts may be shown out of chronological order; that does not reorder their occurrence.

# Continuity notes

## Established invariants

1. Coriolanus Snow and Edmund Voss are one man. Voss is an acquired public identity, not another personality. [Snow VI]
2. Use young Tom Blyth Snow. Love and tenderness are real; so are possessiveness, entitlement and harm. Do not flatten him into either an innocent romantic hero or a caricature. [II]
3. The Underground relationship was genuinely mutual and happy for a meaningful period. Snow was more openly affectionate; Levi genuinely reciprocated. Do not retroactively make every past gesture a scheme. [III]
4. The breakup is about incompatible moral choices affecting others, not poverty, Levi's naivety or fear Snow would kill him. Its specific precipitating event remains open. [IV]
5. Levi could have killed Snow, spared him, provided a way aboveground and told him never to return. Levi meant a permanent goodbye. [IV.4]
6. Keep three peaceful village years followed by five years of deliberate reinvention. Snow is capable of a life that is not constant obsession. [V]
7. At Eren's trial both recognize each other immediately. Snow's public presence has a legitimate political rationale; details still need approval. [VII]
8. Erwin and Levi are NOT already a couple. Their growing closeness does not grant Snow a claim over Levi. [VII.4; XII.21–24]
9. Snow returns expecting renewed love, not revenge. Levi has moved forward and owes no renewed relationship. Past intimacy is not present consent. [I; VIII; X]
10. Avoid unlimited political authority, generic villain speeches or an opening backstory dump. [VI; IX; XI–XII]

## Source authority and conflicts

Current author instructions govern preparation and Chapter One preservation. The Snow dossier governs its AU-specific continuity; the general bible supplies compatible characterization. *Power to Strive* is an external reference, not an established Snow chapter or automatic canon.

- **Resolved by source specificity:** Snow's immediately-pre-trial room opening supersedes the base bible's two-days-before-the-57th-Expedition opening. Reassess what each character has actually experienced at the earlier point.
- **Explicit override:** “Erwin and Levi are NOT a couple” must survive any import of the general bible or app's unrelated relationship rules.
- **UNRESOLVED:** exact first-meeting date versus eight years apart; see TIMELINE.
- **UNRESOLVED:** exact role/authority of Voss, roster, display names and revealed knowledge in an already-approved Chapter One.
- **Scope correction:** “The characters do not know Snow” in XI cannot erase Levi's own memories. Levi knows his past; the uninformed viewers discover it.
- **Possible wording tension:** eight years of return-narrative construction versus three peaceful years and five deliberate years. Do not silently replace the latter.

## Chapter preservation

**UNRESOLVED:** no approved Snow Chapter One text is available. No Snow chapter has been rewritten, paraphrased or replaced. Preservation can be certified only after receiving its exact file and hashing it. No story passage is generated as a placeholder.

**PROPOSED workflow:** each approved chapter should have an original, an author approval record, a content hash, and a separate continuity entry listing events, state changes, who learned what and unresolved threads. Earlier drafts remain distinct and intact.

# Relationships

[III] | Exact meeting, courtship, home details and relationship duration remain open. Do not retroactively make all affection manipulative. |
| Snow ↔ Levi, breakup | Incompatible moral choices; Levi spares him and intends permanent separation. Snow fails to accept the finality. [IV] | Triggering incident, affected people and dialogue are not finalized. |
| Snow → Levi, present | Still loves him, remembers ordinary details, expects a renewed future and returns from a sense of coming home. [VIII; X] | Love is not entitlement or present consent. No automatic reconciliation. |
| Levi → Snow, present | Recognizes him immediately; remembers a meaningful past; has built his own life and can refuse him. [VII–VIII] | Possible nostalgia or tenderness is not a promise of renewed romance. Exact response belongs to unwritten/unsupplied chapters. |
| Erwin ↔ Levi | Comrades and colleagues with trust and growing emotional closeness; NOT an established couple. [VII.4; XII] | Do not import the Your Name AU's established relationship. Future outcome is not established. |
